content.title: About
content.content: Beef is the meat of cattle, obtained from various cuts of the animal's carcass. It is rich in protein, iron, zinc, and B‑vitamins. Beef is used worldwide in dishes ranging from steaks and roasts to soups and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef has been a staple food for humans since prehistoric times.
Different cuts have distinct flavors and textures: tenderloin is the most tender, while brisket is tougher but flavorful when slow‑cooked.
In Japan, thinly sliced raw beef (gyu‑sashimi) is a delicacy served as sushi.
Quality is often judged by marbling – the amount of intramuscular fat that makes the meat juicier.
In countries like Argentina, beef is a national dish and a major export commodity.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is highly bioavailable, helping prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals boost immune function and protect against oxidative stress.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine in beef can improve muscular performance and endurance.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Consuming large amounts of fatty beef cuts may raise cholesterol levels and cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked or raw beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella; cook to safe internal temperatures.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Beef is high in purines, which can exacerbate gout in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergy and sensitivity
items.content: Although rare, some people may experience allergic reactions to beef.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beef can be grilled, pan‑seared, braised, roasted, or boiled. Thin steaks are ideal for quick searing, while larger cuts benefit from slow cooking in sauces. Ground beef is commonly used for burgers, meatballs, and pie fillings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh beef in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in airtight packaging at –18 °C; quality is maintained for 6‑12 months. Thaw frozen beef in the fridge, not at room temperature.
